'''Heike Hofmann''' (born 16 April 1972) is a [[Statistics|statistician]] and Professor in the Department of Statistics at [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]] and was previously at [[Iowa State University]].<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stat.iastate.edu/people/heike-hofmann|title = Heike Hofmann}}</ref><ref>[http://visiphilia.org/ Visiphilia: The love of plotting data] (shared blog with [[Dianne Cook (statistician)|Dianne Cook]])</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://directory.unl.edu/people/hhofmann4 |title=Heike Hofmann |website=University of Nebraska–Lincoln |access-date=2024-10-12}}</ref>

==Education==
She earned an [[Master of Science|MSc]] in Mathematics, with a minor in Computer Science, and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in Statistics,  from the [[University of Augsburg]], [[Augsburg]], [[Germany]] in 1998 and 2000, respectively.<ref name=mathgene/>

==Career and research==
Hofmann's research interests are in [[statistical graphics]], [[Data science|exploratory data analysis]], [[Inference|visual inference]], [[Data visualization|visualization of large data]] and [[statistical computing]]<ref name=gs/><ref name="HofmannSiebes2000">{{cite book|last1=Hofmann|first1=Heike|last2=Siebes|first2=Arno P. J. M.|last3=Wilhelm|first3=Adalbert F. X.|title=Proceedings of the sixth ACM SIGKDD international conference on Knowledge discovery and data mining - KDD '00|chapter=Visualizing association rules with interactive mosaic plots|year=2000|pages=227–235|doi=10.1145/347090.347133|isbn=1581132336|s2cid=1158773}}</ref><ref name="BujaSwayne2008">{{cite journal|last1=Buja|first1=Andreas|last2=Swayne|first2=Deborah F|last3=Littman|first3=Michael L|last4=Dean|first4=Nathaniel|last5=Hofmann|first5=Heike|last6=Chen|first6=Lisha|title=Data Visualization With Multidimensional Scaling|journal=Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics|volume=17|issue=2|year=2008|pages=444–472|issn=1061-8600|doi=10.1198/106186008X318440|s2cid=10675294}}</ref> She is currently{{when|date=July 2021}} Professor in the Department of Statistics at [[Iowa State University]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stat.iastate.edu|publisher=Iowa State University|accessdate=2 November 2016|title=Department of Statistics web site}}</ref> and faculty member of the [[Bioinformatics]] and [[Computational Biology]] and [[Human Computer Interaction]] programs.

In her research on [[interactive data visualization]] she has provided new approaches for plotting [[Multivariate analysis|multivariate]] [[categorical data]] using [[mosaic plot]]s, and making interactions with these plots, and linking between plots. She was the primary development of the software [https://rosuda.org/MANET/ MANET] and contributed to the development of the software [[GGobi]]. More recent software include the [[R (programming language)|R]] packages x3prplus, geomnet, nullabor, gglogo, peptider, discreteRV, ggboxplots, ggparallel, dbData, HLMdiag, lvboxplots, MergeGUI, MissingDataGUI. Her work on examining the inflow of corporate cash into the 2012 US presidential election can be read in [[Chance (statistics magazine)|''Chance'' magazine]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://chance.amstat.org/2014/02/president/|publisher=American Statistical Association|accessdate=2 November 2016|title=Can You Buy a President? Politics After the Tillman Act}}</ref>

Heike Hofmann is the author of more than 50 journal articles, conference proceedings, book chapters and edited one book. She is a Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]]. She has supervised or co-supervised 8 doctoral theses,<ref name=mathgene/> including [[Hadley Wickham]]<ref name=wphd>{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Hadley Alexander|last=Wickham |title=Practical tools for exploring data and models |publisher=Iowa State University |date=2008 |url=https://lib.dr.iastate.edu/rtd/15639/|website=iastate.edu |oclc=247410260|id={{ProQuest|194000416}} |doi=10.31274/rtd-180813-16852 |hdl=|doi-access=free }}</ref> and [[Yihui Xie]].<ref name=yphd/>

===Honors and awards===
She was elected a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2014.<ref name=amstat>{{Cite web |url=https://www.amstat.org/ASA/Your-Career/Awards/ASA-Fellows-list.aspx |title=ASA Fellows List |access-date=2 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190425013824/https://www.amstat.org/ASA/Your-Career/Awards/ASA-Fellows-list.aspx |archive-date=25 April 2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
